messages:
alex: Customer reports intermittent 401s when calling hosted API over AWS PrivateLink + central egress TGW. Works sometimes, but high-volume clients get 401s for a few minutes then recover. They say nothing changed in app.
maria: Can you paste a minimal repro curl + the Host header they send and the dig output for api.redwood.com from their app host? Also route table + VPCE config.
alex: Repro curl and dig below. app host is an EC2 in a spoke VPC that egresses via central TGW+NAT. VPCE is interface-type in spoke. Repro (sanitized):
```
curl -v -H "Authorization: Bearer REDACTED" -H "Host: api.redwood.com" https://api.redwood.com/v1/health
* Connected to 10.10.12.34 (10.10.12.34) port 443 (#0)
* TLS handshake completed, server certificate: CN = internal-nlb.local
> GET /v1/health HTTP/1.1
> Host: api.redwood.com
> Authorization: Bearer REDACTED
< HTTP/1.1 401 Unauthorized
{
  "error": "invalid_audience"
}
```
```
$ dig +short api.redwood.com
10.10.12.34
```
Note: when they temporarily change the app to egress directly to internet (bypass TGW/NAT), calls succeed with 200. When routed via TGW/NAT we see 401s.
sam: Interesting. Two quick theories: 1) DNS split-horizon mismatch + TLS/SNI cert mismatch causing backend to treat request as unknown host (audience mismatch). 2) SNAT from NAT changes source IP; maybe there's an allowlist or token bound to IP or to a specific Host header that the proxy rewrites. Do you have VPCE policy or NLB target-group healthcheck logs?
paul: Also confirm NLB is preserving SNI and Host header. If the NLB/ALB or any proxy is terminating TLS and re-issuing TLS to the backend with a different server_name, the API may validate audience against the resolved host.
alex: VPCE config snippet:
```
aws ec2 describe-vpc-endpoints --vpc-endpoint-ids vpce-0abc1234
{ "VpcEndpointId": "vpce-0abc1234", "ServiceName": "com.amazonaws.vpce.us-east-1.vpce-svc-abcdef", "PrivateDnsEnabled": true }
```
Route table from spoke (relevant):
```
0.0.0.0/0 -> tgw-attach-rt
10.10.0.0/16 -> local
```
TGW attachment to central has a default route to a NAT GW for internet egress. The VPCE IP is in 10.10.12.0/24 and targets are NLB ENIs.
maria: Can you tcpdump the TLS handshake and post the ClientHello SNI and the server cert CN/SAN? If the SNI is api.redwood.com but the server presents internal-nlb.local, that's a mismatch.
alex: Captured server cert shows CN=internal-nlb.local and SAN includes internal-nlb.local only. ClientHello SNI=api.redwood.com. So the NLB is terminating TLS to backend and backend serves internal cert. But when egress via internet it hits the public gateway (CloudFront/proxy) with proper cert for api.redwood.com and 200.
paul: That explains invalid_audience. The API validates the incoming TLS peer cert or Host, or we're seeing a header rewrite at the central proxy that changes the Host to internal. Why only intermittent? Could be path: sometimes traffic stays within VPC path to public egress (direct to public listener) and other times hits internal NLB due to routing asymmetry or ephemeral healthcheck failover.
sam: Check the VPCE endpoint policy and route propagation. If the central TGW sends some traffic out through NAT, SNAT restores 52.x.x.x -> public GW path with correct cert; if the path hairpins to the NLB (ENI -> local target group) you'll hit internal cert. Also confirm security groups on NLB targets allow traffic from TGW ENI IP ranges; if not, traffic may be dropped or retried via alternate path.
alex: Looking at ALB/NLB target group health, targets show healthy but occasional 502s in a couple AZs. Also found VPCE DNS: the VPC resolver returns 10.10.12.34 (internal NLB) due to PrivateDnsEnabled. Customer had mistakenly added an override in central resolver conditional-forwarder pointing api.redwood.com to the internal IP in some spoke accounts, causing split-horizon inconsistencies.
maria: Actionable checklist:
- Remove the conditional-forwarder override so VPCE private DNS resolves consistently to VPCE private IPs only in spokes that should use them.
- Ensure NLB is configured for TLS passthrough (preserve cert) or use proper cert with SAN api.redwood.com on internal path.
- Confirm token/audience checks are not tied to source IP; if they are, update allowlist to include TGW NAT IPs.
- Add route in spoke RT for the VPCE IP range -> local ENI to avoid hairpin via TGW.
paul: Also check endpoint policy: make sure it's not restricting which principals or VPCs can call the service. If endpoint policy denies some requests intermittently because of route flaps, you'll see auth-like failures.
alex: Customer applied two changes: fixed conditional-forwarder and added route for VPCE CIDR to local ENI. After that they reported 24h without 401s. They also rotated the internal cert to include api.redwood.com SAN as a fallback in case of internal termination.
sam: Nice. For postmortem, capture:
- pcap of a failing case (ClientHello, ServerCert)
- dig +trace from app host
- route table dump and vpce describe output
- NLB listener config (tls passthrough vs terminate)
deploy-bot: Note: created ticket INF-8342 to track follow-up: update docs for VPCE + TGW egress patterns and recommended NLB TLS config.
alex: Customer satisfied. Closing for now but asked for short doc we can share. I'll draft a runbook with the checklist above.
maria: Thanks — please ping if it reappears. :thumbsup:
